title: Represent and Describe Data in a Histogram

items.stem: What does each bar in a histogram represent?
choices: The frequency of data values within a range
The total number of all data points combined
The average of all data points

items.stem: A histogram shows the number of books students read last month in these intervals: 0–2, 3–5, 6–8, and 9–11. If the bar for 3–5 books reaches a height of 7, what does this tell you?
choices: 7 students read a number of books between 3 and 5, inclusive.
7 books were read in total by the students.
The average number of books read was 7.

items.stem: Look at a histogram showing the ages of students in a class divided into groups 10–12, 13–15, and 16–18. Which of the following statements are true about this histogram? (Select ALL that apply.)
choices: The bars represent the number of students in each age group.
The width of each bar shows the age range covered.
The height of each bar shows the exact age of each student.
There are no gaps between bars because the age intervals are continuous.

items.stem: A teacher collected data on how many minutes six students spent reading each day for one week. She created a histogram with intervals of 10 minutes: 0–9, 10–19, 20–29, 30–39, and 40–49. The tallest bar is in the 20–29 interval with a frequency of 4. Explain what this means about the students’ reading habits. Show or explain your work.
